subject: Prove the quasi-invariance of the extremal width and of the moduli of a nest under C¹ embeddings of bounded dilatation
area_note: The extremal width of a family of curves is at most K times that of any family that contains the images of its curves under a C¹ embedding of dilatation at most K (K = 1 for an injective holomorphic map with non-vanishing derivative), and the image of a nest has annuli with at least 1/K times the moduli, so divergent moduli are transported by a chart of bounded dilatation; the correspondence of the phase–parameter relation is quasi-conformal rather than a C¹ chart, and the construction of the nest from an a priori bound stays open.

subject: Express the fractal dimension against smooth curves: C¹ charts preserve dimension, the Hölder barrier of the boundary of M, and Peano objects of CompHaus
area_note: A C¹ embedding preserves the Hausdorff dimension of every subset, so no C¹ chart carries a smooth curve onto a fractal, and a quasi-conformal map of finite dilatation never carries a set of dimension below 2 onto a set of dimension 2; given Shishikura's theorem (dimension 2 of the boundary of M) the boundary is not covered by countably many smooth loops and has no parametrization by an interval that is Hölder with exponent above 1/2; a kernel of positive dimension forces a finite total modulus while divergent moduli leave a point; local connectivity is stated as an epimorphism from the interval in CompHaus, with the Hahn–Mazurkiewicz theorem as an explicit hypothesis. The dimension decides neither the area of the boundary nor the shrinking of the nests.

subject: Close the chain from collars to local connectivity at a point with a logarithmic scale, show that a level tower has no dynamics by itself, and correct the claims of the moduli stack after an audit
area_note: A set is locally connected at the center of a nest whose moduli add up to infinity (the Yoccoz criterion), and with a uniform lower bound for the moduli the connected neighbourhoods of the center are reached at depth O(log(1/ε)); collars of bounded dilatation and definite modulus at the jumps of a level tower, the linear dichotomy (or, with the Teichmüller contraction, collars at the jumps at large relative period) and the phase–parameter comparison give the local connectivity of M at a parameter; every width tower is realized by round level sets, so a level tower carries no dynamics by itself; an audit corrected the statements on the conformal invariance of the width, the dimension of quasi-conformal images, the quotient form of MLC, the kernel of a nest and the C¹ modulus. The collars, Lemma D, Lemma TC′ and the comparison are not proved.

subject: Derive Lemma D from stacked annuli: p disjoint sub-annuli of definite modulus give the linear dichotomy
area_note: Grötzsch's inequality for pairwise disjoint sub-annuli of an annulus, and the quasi-additivity mechanism of §4.2 in the language of level towers: if the annulus of the level k+n contains p disjoint sub-annuli, each of modulus at least c'/(W_k + A'), then c' p W_{k+n} ≤ W_k + A' and the linear dichotomy holds; with the collars of Lemma G, the Teichmüller contraction and the phase–parameter comparison this gives the local connectivity of M at a parameter, and every hypothesis but the Teichmüller contraction is a statement about moduli of annuli; the sub-annuli, pullbacks of the shallower annulus along the critical orbit, are not constructed.
